subject: Q3 OKR pulse: heatmap, runway asks, and dependency plan
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q3 OKR pulse: heatmap, runway asks, and dependency plan

Team —

Attached is a compact heatmap (Q3_OKR_heatmap_v2.xlsx) and a dependency matrix that I prepared for our mid-quarter check. TL;DR: overall progress remains green on Platform Reliability and Hosted API adoption, but Objective 2 (Latency and Serving Cost) is amber due to two blockers we didn’t surface broadly: a) suboptimal batching config on Dedicated pools for long-tail seqs and b) an unresolved kernel fallback that hits NVLink on certain infra.

Key asks:
- Approve scope 2.1 re-scope: drop non-essential perf experiments (benchmarks for experimental kernels) and reallocate 0.6 FTE from R&D to Ops to stabilize configs for the next 6 weeks.
- Marcus/Infra: need a firmer ETA for kernel fallback mitigation (see dependency_matrix.csv). If we can’t land by 8/12, I recommend we pin a conservative routing policy to avoid NVLink path for high-priority tenants.
- Monica/Partnerships: ask CloudOps partner for a short-term capacity boost on our Dedicated pool week of 7/27 (they’ve tentatively agreed, need confirmation). Sam at Acme flagged this as a risk for their integration timeline.

Attached notes include a suggested runway resource request PDF; if we get leadership buy-in today, I’ll file the procurement request and send the doc to Finance.

Proposed next steps: two options — quick async approvals (reply-all with thumbs) OR a 30-minute sync at 3:30pm PT today to lock decisions. I prefer the sync given the infra uncertainty, but will proceed with whichever you folks pick.

Thanks —
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: Q3_OKR_heatmap_v2.xlsx, dependency_matrix.csv, runway_resource_requests.pdf)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 OKR pulse: heatmap, runway asks, and dependency plan

Thanks Rachel — useful distillation.

Quick clarifying asks before I sign off on the re-scope:
- Can you quantify the expected delta in latency and cost if we pause the experimental kernel benchmarks? A short table (baseline vs paused) will help me justify the temporary reallocation to Finance.
- Marcus: if the NVLink fallback remains, what’s the expected % of requests that will see >100ms regression? I want to know how many SLAs could be impacted.

I’m available for the 3:30pm sync but if we can resolve these two numbers asynchronously I’ll pre-approve the scope change.

Vivek
VP Product
(Attachment: none)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 13:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 OKR pulse: heatmap, runway asks, and dependency plan

Rachel — good summary. A few inline notes: 

> drop non-essential perf experiments (benchmarks for experimental kernels)

Agree with temporary pause but we should keep one minimal experiment running to detect regressions early (low QPS, isolated test tenants).

> need a firmer ETA for kernel fallback mitigation

Marcus — please include an entry in the dependency matrix with: ETA, owner, mitigation plan (short & long), and customer impact estimate. Vivek, I can prep the justification numbers for Finance once we have Marcus’s customer impact % and your latency/cost delta.

Also Monica — if CloudOps partner confirms a week-of boost, please flag any extra cost and whether Acme is willing to share partial incremental cost (they were receptive during last sync).

If we can get Marcus’s ETA and Vivek’s delta by 3pm PT I’ll skip the sync and approve the re-scope.

—Laura
Director, Growth Ops
(Attachment: none)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 OKR pulse: heatmap, runway asks, and dependency plan

Thanks all — quick updates and commitments: 

- Marcus: ETA 2026-08-10 for a staged kernel fix; mitigation (pin routing) ready by 7/28. Marcus confirmed in Slack and entered the details into dependency_matrix.csv (row 7).
- Vivek: I attached a short delta table in runway_resource_requests.pdf — expected median latency impact for affected requests is +85ms (p95 +240ms) if we do not patch; cost delta for pausing the experimental kernels is ~ +2.1% net (we lose a small optimization pathway but avoid the NVLink penalty).
- Monica: CloudOps confirmed tentative capacity boost; Monica to get a signed change order today and will confirm by EOD. Acme (Sam) is looped for visibility on the customer timeline.

Decision: moving forward with the temporary re-scope for Objective 2.1. Action items:
1) Rachel — file procurement for 0.6 FTE ops support and change order (will do by EOD).
2) Marcus — implement conservative routing pin and share monitors by 7/28.
3) Monica — confirm CloudOps change order and cost split with Acme by EOD.
4) Vivek & Laura — finalize Finance justification using the attached runway PDF; we’ll target sign-off by 7/24.

I’ll close the loop after procurement submission. If anything changes, reply-all. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

Rachel
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: runway_resource_requests.pdf)
